Recent work supports combining item text with collaborative signals, but does not establish a ready-made solution under the no-pretraining constraint. [Recformer (2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) jointly learns language and sequential recommendation representations, using a Transformer backbone. [TედRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) identifies limitations of directly adding text and ID embeddings; its sequence-level Fourier fusion is equivalent to contextual convolution. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates titles, descriptions and reviews through BERT, with reviews contributing most—its reported gains therefore do not directly transfer to this task’s available inputs or initialization restrictions.

Product text can describe functionality, but complementarity and substitution require careful supervision. [Amazon’s SIGIR 2023 substitute model](https://www.amazon.science/publications/a-transformer-based-substitute-recommendation-model-incorporating-weakly-supervised-customer-behavior-data) matches title/description text while denoising behavioral supervision; it does not establish that semantic similarity alone identifies substitutes. A constraint-compatible hypothesis, rather than a demonstrated result from these papers: randomly initialize a small word/subword embedding encoder with pooling or text CNN, learn a gated residual fusion with item-ID embeddings, and jointly optimize it inside the existing causal NextItNet using next-item supervision. Shared text parameters could help sparse items, while the gate limits noisy descriptions. Preserve one network/checkpoint per category; treat compatibility and purchase intent as latent hypotheses, never observed labels. Validate any benefit through the fixed macro HR@10 protocol.
